findings.reason: the plan already names and extends the owner, reset_to_status already takes an extra_filter scoping hook but the re-expand case (a root already at status triaged) is not a status transition it can express, so the seed clear is a defensible second entry point rather than a fork, and the author would decline with that reason.
findings.text: the section makes the seed item clear expanded_at on an explicit --root reseed, a second writer of the field that imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:PATH_RESET_SPECS owns (it gains expanded_at in clear_fields for its scanned/triaged specs), so the field that makes a path reprocessable is now cleared in two places that must stay in agreement

findings.reason: both uncited sites read the chunk's own source_file, which the plan elsewhere acknowledges is populated and correct, so they carry no null-source defect; the finding only asks the author to state that scope, not to change the mechanism.
findings.text: the section's inventory states "Five readers exist today" but a sixth and seventh site resolve a CodeChunk's source and are not cited: _vector_search_code_chunks joins "(cf:CodeFile {path: cc.source_file})" and imas_codex/ids/tools.py:715 joins (cf)-[:HAS_EXAMPLE]->(ce)-[:HAS_CHUNK]->(cc), so the stated invariant "every reader resolves a chunk's source through one owner" is broader than the five sites the design repairs

duplicate_owner-1.reason: The reset spec owns status transitions; an already-triaged root re-expanding is not a transition, so the explicit --root seed is a second entry point that the section names and tests beside the owner, not a fork.

reuse_search-1.reason: _vector_search_code_chunks and ids/tools.py read the chunk's own populated source_file and carry no null-source defect; the brief states that scope so the worker leaves them alone.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §19 adds one parameterised renderer to imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py (a module that already composes relationship traversals) that hides the HAS_CHUNK OPTIONAL MATCH plus coalesce behind a single alias/output-name interface, and §14 adds no new module at all, extending the seed item and the reset owner in place; neither section spreads a mechanism across new wide-shallow surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §14 clears expanded_at inside seed_facility_roots beside the reset owner that owns the reprocessability stamp.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §19 adds one slot-annotation key (inverse_of) and one renderer and, in its own text, names the three relationship names it retires (CODE_EXAMPLE_ID, WIKI_PAGE_ID, DOCUMENT_ID) plus the dead CodeFile-[:HAS_CHUNK] arm, and §14 adds no public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — both live design sections cite the machinery they extend rather than proposing a subsystem blind: §14 names seed_facility_roots/persist_scan_results/claim_paths_for_expanding (imas_codex/discovery/paths/frontier.py) and PATH_RESET_SPECS (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:240), and §19 names the five divergent chunk-source readers, GraphSchema.relationships (imas_codex/graph/schema.py:109) and query_builder._parse_traverse/graph_search; the only prior-art gap I found is recorded as a finding.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the §19 renderer is new consolidating machinery over five divergent call sites, not a layer over one existing mechanism whose extension would do; §19 states why the resolution cannot live in imas_codex/ingestion (four of five readers sit in the graph and llm layers above it), which is the justification the item asks a wrapper to give.
